aligned_segments.en: Oy vey — it is impossible to tell everything in detail. But the main thing — let me begin to tell what passed over me, how Hashem had mercy upon me and arranged the circumstances so that I would merit drawing close to our holy Rabbenu.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, וּמֵהַלַּיְלָה הַזּוֹ נַעֲשָׂה רַעַשׁ בִּטְבֶרְיָה: "הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער בְּרֶסְלְבֶר!"
aligned_segments.en: I was learning in the yeshiva in Teveriah, at the tomb of Rabbi Meir Ba'al HaNes — it stands among the fields and the mountains. I loved to go out and wander between the mountains and the fields, even before I drew close to Rabbenu. When I became seventeen years old I had very difficult battles with the yetzer hora. What to do? I still did not know of Rabbenu. So Hashem arranged that I went out of the yeshiva to the courtyard to fetch a glass of tea — and in the courtyard stood a garbage bin. I saw there sacred texts [pages with G-d's Name]. It was an old book without a cover, without a beginning, without an end — just pages with Names of G-d on them.

aligned_segments.he: בַּבֹּקֶר שֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לְבֵית-כְּנֶסֶת וְרַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה בַּבֵּית-כְּנֶסֶת וַאֲנִי דִּבַּרְתִּי אִתּוֹ וְלָמַדְנוּ סִפְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ וּגְמָרָא וְשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ, פּוֹסְקִים, אָז תֵּכֶף נַעֲשָׂה רַעַשׁ גָּדוֹל בִּטְבֶרְיָה וְיָצָא לִי שֵׁם שֶׁאֲנִי נֶעֱשֵׂיתִי בְּרֶסְלְבֶר.
aligned_segments.en: Now, I was God-fearing — so in order that the book not be degraded amidst the garbage, I took the book with the intention of placing it in the genizah [the repository for sacred texts] in the yeshiva. Before I threw it into the genizah, I saw that the name of the book was Hishtapchus HaNefesh ["The Outpouring of the Soul"]…

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, עָבַר עָלַי מַחֲלֹקֶת, מִלְחָמָה גְּדוֹלָה, וְהָאַבָּא וְהָאִמָּא וְהַקְּרוֹבִים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּחָה וְכָל הַיְשִׁיבָה, כֻּלָּם אָמְרוּ: "אוֹי וֵוי רַחֲמָנוּת גָדוֹל, יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער נַעֲשָׂה בְּרֶסְלְבֶר, יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער נַעֲשָׂה בְּרֶסְלְבֶר!" כֻּלָּם הִתְנַגְּדוּ.
aligned_segments.en: Hishtapchus HaNefesh — this made an impression upon me. I had a longing to pour out my soul to Hashem. [Root: שׁפך — to pour out; cf. "I pour out my soul within me" [Psalms 42:5]] Maybe this was suited for me. And also I was accustomed to reading many mussar books, Chassidic books — but I had never seen a book with such a name: Hishtapchus HaNefesh. So I thought to myself: "Perhaps this is good for me. Perhaps this is Providence from Hashem that I should have this book." So I began to read — I read one page… and immediately I saw that this was very good for me, that it was from Heaven. I saw that it was a kindness from Hashem that I had merited finding this book — because every word was for me, and I would succeed in conquering all the battles, all that I was suffering. So I did not throw the book into the genizah. I took it — and I "stole myself away" from the yeshiva to the field between the mountains with the book, and I began to read…

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, הֵם הָלְכוּ מֵהַיְשִׁיבָה לְהַהוֹרִים וְסִפְּרוּ לָהֶם: "אַתֶּם יוֹדְעִים, יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער נַעֲשָׂה בְּרֶסְלְבֶר".
aligned_segments.en: From the time I found the book, I would go with it to do hisbodidus, and I prayed as it described in the name of Rabbenu — how to do hisbodidus and how to pray. I walked through the fields, no one knew — it was like a theft; I stole myself away to the fields. I had hisbodidus, I read in the book, and I fulfilled what was written there.

aligned_segments.he: וְהָאַבָּא וְהָאִמָּא שָׁמְעוּ וְלֹא הִקְפִּידוּ כָּל-כָּךְ, אֲבָל בָּא אֲלֵיהֶם הַגַּבַּאי שֶׁל הַיְשִׁיבָה וְעוֹד אֲנָשִׁים נִכְבָּדִים, לַמְדָּנִים וּבַעֲלֵי-שֵׁם וּפִרְסוּם, וְאָמְרוּ לְהָאַבָּא: "אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער נַעֲשָׂה בְּרֶסְלְבֶר!"
aligned_segments.en: And I saw — for the first time in my life — the power of this book. What power of hisbodidus! It slays all the destroyers, all the harmful forces, all kinds of evil sicknesses, all kinds of deeds, all kinds of desires.

aligned_segments.he: אָז אָמַר אַבָּא: "אֲנִי לֹא דּוֹאֵג, אֲנִי מַכִּיר אֶת הַבֵּן שֶׁלִּי, הוּא יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם וְהוּא מְקַיֵּם כִּבּוּד אָב הֲכִי בָּעוֹלָם, אֲפִלּוּ שֶׁאֲנִי אֶשְׁלַח אוֹתוֹ לָאֵשׁ - הוּא יֵלֵךְ, אֵין דֻּגְמָתוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: I saw with my own eyes that after hisbodidus, when I returned to the yeshiva, I was like a new person.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי לֹא מֻדְאָג.
aligned_segments.en: I felt within myself: "Where are all the destroyers?

aligned_segments.he: אָז כְּשֶׁהוּא יָבוֹא מֵהַיְשִׁיבָה אֲנִי אַגִּיד לוֹ שֶׁאֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה, אָז הוּא לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּרֶסְלְבֶר. אֵין לִי שׁוּם בְּעָיָה".
aligned_segments.en: They have been slain!"

aligned_segments.he: אָז הֵם אָמְרוּ: "אַתָּה לֹא יוֹדֵעַ מַה זֶּה בְּרֶסְלֶב, הוּא לֹא יִשְׁמַע לְךָ, אַתָּה צָרִיךְ מִלְחָמָה כְּבֵדָה".
aligned_segments.en: Until that point, because I had wanted to save myself from the yetzer hora, I had searched and searched and searched. And although I had had certain salvations, a salvation of this kind — to conquer all the battles with ease — I had never experienced. I read within the book one page, two pages — and immediately I fulfilled what was written there. And I saw such wonders as I had never seen in all my days of life! I had searched in books and found salvation — but something like this, such a wonder within the words of this book, I had never known!

aligned_segments.he: אָז אָמַר: "אֲנִי לֹא דּוֹאֵג, אֲנִי מַכִּיר אֶת בְּנִי".
aligned_segments.en: I studied greatly in the book, with arousal and fervor. But I did not know who was the author of the book — because it was just pages, and the pages were to me like a treasure. I locked the book inside a box, and every day I had this practice: I went with the book to the field and read — and immediately fulfilled what I had read — and I saw such wonders! The nullification of nature!

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי בָּאתִי מֵהַיְשִׁיבָה בְּיוֹם חֲמִישִׁי, אָז אָמַר לִי אַבָּא: "תֵּדַע בְּנִי שֶׁהָיָה אֶצְלִי הַגְּדוֹלִים מֵהַיְשִׁיבָה וְאָמְרוּ לִי שֶׁאַתָּה נַעֲשֵׁיתָ בְּרֶסְלֵב.
aligned_segments.en: I saw great wonders that I had never known.

aligned_segments.he: תֵּדַע בְּנִי, רַחֵם עָלַי, אֲנִי מְבַקֵּשׁ אוֹתְךָ שֶׁלֹּא לְצַעֵר אוֹתִי, אַתָּה שַׁיָּךְ לַחֲסִידוּת אַחֶרֶת, וַאֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ רְשׁוּת לִהְיוֹת בְּאֵיזֶה חֲסִידוּת שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה, רַק בַּקָּשָׁה אַחַת יֵשׁ לִי, אֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה בְּרֶסְלְבֶר".
aligned_segments.en: I saw new miracles and marvels, the like of which — from the day I came to my senses — I had never seen. And I did not know who the author of the book was…

aligned_segments.he: אָז זֶה הַפַּעַם הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁעָבַרְתִּי עַל מִצְוַת כִּבוּד אָב וְאָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: "אַבָּא, אַתָּה מַכִּיר אוֹתִי, אֲנִי מְקַיֵּם כִּבּוּד אָב, הַכֹּל אֲנִי אֶשְׁמַע לְךָ, רַק הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה - לֹא! בָּזֶה אֲנִי לֹא אֶשְׁמַע לְךָ! מַדּוּעַ? אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ".
aligned_segments.en: One time I was sitting on my bed reading the book and a friend from my Chassidic group came and saw me reading with fervor, with seriousness, with love and great awakening in the book. He saw that the book was Hishtapchus HaNefesh, and he knew that it was from the Breslov books. So this friend said to me: "What are you doing?! You are reading from this book?! It is forbidden to read from this book — it is from the Breslov books!"

aligned_segments.he: אָז הוּא רָאָה: "אַהָהּ, הַצֶּדֶק אִתָּם.
aligned_segments.en: But I had already tasted the taste of the book and had seen the wonders. I was stunned and became very angry, and entered into a great rage, and I said to him: "This is none of your business, you wicked one!

aligned_segments.he: הֵם אָמְרוּ שֶׁאֲנִי לֹא יוֹדֵעַ מַה זֶּה בְּרֶסְלֶב, מַה זֶּה! זֶה נוֹרָא מְאֹד, הוּא מְקַיֵּם כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו כִּבּוּד אָב בִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ וְעַכְשָׁו הוּא אוֹמֵר כָּךְ? זֶה פַּעַם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּחַיָּי שֶׁאֲנִי שׁוֹמֵעַ שֶׁלֹּא רוֹצֶה לְקַיֵּם אֶת דִּבּוּרִי".
aligned_segments.en: About this book you say it is forbidden to learn?! You do not know what there is in the world! This book is holy of holies — and I see from it great wonders!"

aligned_segments.he: הָאַבָּא אָמַר לִי: "אֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה בְּרֶסְלֶב בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן! אֲנִי רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה כְּמוֹ כָּל הָעוֹלָם".
aligned_segments.en: So he said to me: "You fool! You are an animal — you are not a human being! You know nothing of what goes on in the world! This is from the Breslov books — it is forbidden to read them. All the Admorim and all the world oppose Breslov and say it is forbidden to read Breslov books!"

aligned_segments.he: אוֹי, אוֹי, מַה שֶּׁהָיָה עוֹד, מַה שֶּׁהָיָה..
aligned_segments.en: I heard for the first time in my life that there was such a thing as Breslov in the world, and that it was forbidden to read their books.

aligned_segments.he: אֶפְשָׁר לְסַפֵּר? כָּל טְבֶרְיָה בָּכוּ עָלַי, הָאַבָּא וְהָאִמָּא שֶׁלִּי בָּכוּ: "מַה שֶּׁנַּעֲשָׂה מִמֶּנּוּ, מַה זֶּה? אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת חָסִיד לֹא בְּרֶסְלֶב.
aligned_segments.en: So I said to him: "I do not obey the entire world, not all the Admorim! Let all the Admorim and all the kings come — I will not listen to anyone!

aligned_segments.he: מַה זֶּה, אֲנַחְנוּ לֹא רוֹצִים בְּרֶסְלֶב!"
aligned_segments.en: This book is good for me. I have seen such wonders that cannot be told!"

aligned_segments.he: הָאַבָּא וְהָאִמָּא וְהַמִּשְׁפָּחָה אָמְרוּ: "זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר, זֶה רַק כִּשּׁוּף. בְּרֶסְלֶב זֶה כִּשּׁוּף!"
aligned_segments.en: He said to me: "You are such an insolent one, so brazen against all the Admorim — then you are not a human being!"

aligned_segments.he: וְכָכָה הָיָה כֻּלָּם, כָּל הַלּוֹמְדִים וְכֻלָּם צָחֲקוּ: "בְּרֶסְלֶב, בְּרֶסְלֶב, בְּרֶסְלֶב.."
aligned_segments.en: I said to him: "For me, this is good!"

aligned_segments.he: רַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל קָרְדוֹנֶר אָמַר לְאִמָּא שֶׁלִּי: "זֶה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן לְבַטֵּל.
aligned_segments.en: So he said: "This book is mine and I want it.

aligned_segments.he: יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער יִהְיֶה לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד בְּרֶסְלֶב וְכָכָה יִהְיֶה!"
aligned_segments.en: I don't need it — I only want you not to read it. I want the book!"

aligned_segments.he: אִמִּי שָׁמְעָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר כָּךְ, אָז הִיא נָפְלָה וּמֵתָה מִגֹּדֶל הַפַּחַד וְהַשֶּׁבֶר הַגָּדוֹל בְּבֵית רַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, הִיא נִפְטְרָה.
aligned_segments.en: I did not want to give it to him.

aligned_segments.he: הִיא שָׁמְעָה שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲזֹר שׁוּם כֹּחַ בָּעוֹלָם. אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי: "אֲנִי אֶהְיֶה בְּרֶסְלֶב כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּי!"
aligned_segments.en: I said to him: "I merited it from hefker [ownerless property] — the book was in the garbage bin."

aligned_segments.he: וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה נֵס מֵהַשָּׁמַיִם.
aligned_segments.en: So he struck me and said: "You are so brazen against all the Admorim, against our Rebbe!

aligned_segments.he: אֶחָד מֵחֶבְרָה קַדִּישָׁא רָאָה שֶׁהָאִמָּא שֶׁלִּי עָשְׂתָה אֵיזֶה תְּנוּעָה מֵהָעַיִן וְהָיָה סִימַן חַיִּים, הוּא רָאָה שֶׁהָעַיִן לֹא מֵת. אֲבָל הוּא חָשַׁב: "זֶה רַק דִּמְיוֹן".
aligned_segments.en: All of them say it is forbidden to read a Breslov book, and you want to read?!"

aligned_segments.he: אָז בָּא עוֹד אֶחָד וְרָאָה גַּם-כֵּן אוֹתוֹ הַדָּבָר, שֶׁהִיא עָשְׂתָה אֵיזֶה תְּנוּעָה בָּעַיִן.
aligned_segments.en: I was unwilling to give him the book in any way — but he was stronger than me and he seized the book from me by force and left.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, "עַל-פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים יָקוּם דָּבָר!"
aligned_segments.en: And I was left an orphan, without the book.

aligned_segments.he: הָאֲנָשִׁים אָמְרוּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לִהְיוֹת בַּחַיִּים, הַלֵּב הִפְסִיק לִפְעֹל וְכֻלָּם רָאוּ שֶׁהִיא מֵתָה, אֲבָל הִיא אָמְרָה: "לֹא, אֲנִי לֹא מֵתָה.."
aligned_segments.en: But there was a certain gain: I had heard that there was a Chassidus in the world called Breslov, and that it was forbidden to study Breslov books. And I had already read in the book several times and tasted its taste. So from what I remembered, I continued to walk in the field and pray and call out to Hashem that He should have mercy on me as He had begun to help me — I had found this book and I know what it did for me — and so He should send me Breslov books and Breslov Chassidim. I want to be a Breslov Chassid!

aligned_segments.he: וְכָל הַחֲסִידִים וְכָל הָעִיר הָיָה כְּבָר רוֹתֵחַ.
aligned_segments.en: I lived in Teveriah and had not gone out from Teveriah. Tzfas [Safed] was close to Teveriah, and everyone traveled to Meron in Elul and on Lag B'Omer.

aligned_segments.he: מִי הָיָה לוֹ הַגְּבוּרָה לְדַבֵּר עִם חֲסִיד בְּרֶסְלֶב אוֹ לִקְרֹא בְּסֵפֶר בְּרֶסְלֶב, הוּא פָּחַד.
aligned_segments.en: But I was poor — I had no money — so I had not traveled to Tzfas. Had I traveled to Tzfas, perhaps I would have heard of Breslov Chassidim.

aligned_segments.he: לָמָה לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת זֶה, זֶה לֹא הָעֵסֶק שֶׁלּוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: But I did not know of Breslov Chassidim. So I begged Hashem to send me Breslov Chassidim.

aligned_segments.he: וּבָרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם, אֲנִי לֹא הִשְׁגַּחְתִּי, לֹא הִסְתַּכַּלְתִּי עַל שׁוּם דָּבָר, לֹא עַל רַבָּנִים גְּדוֹלִים וְלֹא עַל שִׁדּוּךְ, אֲנִי מָסַרְתִּי הַכֹּל רַק מַה שֶּׁרָאִיתִי מַה זֶּה רַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל קָרְדוֹנֶר.
aligned_segments.en: I thought: "Perhaps there are Breslov Chassidim somewhere in the world — perhaps in Yerushalayim." I beseeched and prayed to Hashem — and a long time passed. And Hashem accepted my prayer and sent me to Teveriah — Rabbi Yisroel Kardoner!

aligned_segments.he: עַד הַיּוֹם יֵשׁ לִי שֵׁם, יֵשׁ כְּבָר שְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה שֶׁנִּתְקָרַבְתִּי לְרַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכֻלָּם הָיוּ מִתְנַגְּדִים כָּאֵלֶּה, וַאֲנִי בָּרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם קִבַּלְתִּי כָּל הַכַּדּוּרִים, כָּל הַבִּזְיוֹנוֹת וְכָל הַצָּרוֹת בְּאַהֲבָה בִּגְבוּרָה גְּדוֹלָה וְכֻלָּם נִתְבַּטְּלוּ מִזֶּה.
aligned_segments.en: I had suffered, and Hashem performed wonders with me — the highest kindness. In Tzfas there lived my holy teacher, Rabbi Yisroel Kardoner, and he was such a novelty as does not exist in the world.

aligned_segments.he: הֵם רָאוּ אֶת הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁלִּי, זֶה לֹא בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע, הֵם לֹא הֵבִינוּ אֶת זֶה.
aligned_segments.en: I had grown up among great Chassidim, strict and meticulous in mitzvos — but when I saw this man, I saw that all of them stood outside; none of them knew anything of emunah, of Torah, of Hashem. They all learned — but compared to him, he was singular in the world; there was no one like him!

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי מֵרַב אֶחָד גָּדוֹל בַּתּוֹרָה וְלָמַדְתִּי אִתּוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: But I did not know him and had not heard of him.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, הָיָה נֵס, אִם הוּא אוֹמֵר "בְּרֶסְלֶב לֹא", אָז תֵּכֶף צְרִיכִים לַעֲזֹב.
aligned_segments.en: He was to be found at Meron and did not want to leave Meron.

aligned_segments.he: אֲבָל אֲנִי רָאִיתִי מַה שֶּׁרָאִיתִי, רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק רָאִיתִי אוֹתוֹ פַּעַם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּחַיָּי, לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מִי הוּא זֶה, אָז אָמַרְתִּי: "אוֹי וֵוי, זֶה הָאִישׁ צַדִּיק נִסְתָּר וַאֲנִי צָרִיךְ אוֹתוֹ מְאֹד, אִם הָיָה לִי אֵיזֶה קֶשֶׁר אִתּוֹ הָיִיתִי זוֹכֶה לַעֲבֹד הַשֵּׁם בֶּאֱמֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֲנִי רוֹצֶה".
aligned_segments.en: He served Hashem there in solitude — there was no other creature there. He had the key to the synagogue of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and he was there alone in hisbodidus, and also walked between the mountains to do hisbodidus and to pray, and engaged in avodas Hashem with mesiras nefesh.

aligned_segments.he: עָבַר מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלַי וְעַל רַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, מַה שֶּׁסָּבַלְנוּ...
aligned_segments.en: His family lived in Tzfas, and he was in Meron all week. Every Friday he would go from Meron to Tzfas. Hashem wanted Rabbi Yisroel to go from Meron to Teveriah — to Yisroel Ber — but Rabbi Yisroel would not leave Meron even if given all the money in the world! Leave Meron? Leave such a holy place and go to Teveriah — what would he have in Teveriah? Every place in the world — only Meron. Who would say that Rabbi Yisroel would go to Teveriah?

aligned_segments.he: הָעִקָּר אֵיךְ סִבֵּב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סִבּוֹת, אֵיךְ זָכִיתִי לֵידַע מֵרַבֵּנוּ.
aligned_segments.en: Hashem knew that Rabbi Yisroel would not budge from Meron. What did He do?

aligned_segments.he: רֵאשִׁית כָּל לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מֵרַבֵּנוּ, לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מֵהַשֵּׁם בְּרֶסְלֶב, סִבֵּב שֶׁנּוֹדַע לִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִפְרֵי בְּרֶסְלֶב שֶׁאָסוּר לִקְרֹא בָּהֶם.
aligned_segments.en: He sent him an illness in his hand, and the pains intensified from day to day, from hour to hour — such pain that it was impossible to say a single word; he could not pray or perform any service. And he attributed nothing to the natural order — only to the Providence of the Creator.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי יֶלֶד עָנִי וְהָיִיתִי מְדֻכֶּא מְאֹד וְגַם-כֵּן אֲנִי לֹא הָיִיתִי כִּשְׁרוֹנִי, לֹא הָיָה לִי מֹחַ לִלְמֹד.
aligned_segments.en: When he saw such a thing, he began to consider: perhaps it is the will of the Creator that he go to Teveriah. What would await him in Teveriah? The climate of Teveriah is even hotter than Meron and Tzfas — he would not be healthy there.

aligned_segments.he: עַל-כָּל-פָּנִים מֵהַלַּיְלָה הַזּוֹ וּבָרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם עַד הַיּוֹם אֲנִי מַחֲזִיק מַעֲמָד.
aligned_segments.en: But he would not suffer such intense pains and would be able to pray and engage in the service of Hashem. But even so, despite such acute pain, he had doubts whether to leave Rabbi Shimon and go to Teveriah or not.

aligned_segments.he: הֵם צָחֲקוּ מִמֶּנִּי כֻּלָּם, הַגְּדוֹלִים וְכָל הָרַבָּנִים, "הוּא בְּרֶסְלֶב!" אֲבָל אֲנִי צָחַקְתִּי מֵהֶם, נִצַּחְתִּי אֶת כֻּלָּם, אֲנִי נִשְׁאַרְתִּי וַאֲנִי אֶשָּׁאֵר בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה, אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן לִי מַתָּנָה, לִהְיוֹת עוֹד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה...
aligned_segments.en: For he thought: "How can such a thing be — when a person is in trouble he flees from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai to Teveriah? One must flee to Rabbi Shimon, to pray and to plead for healing." So as long as he did not know with certainty that it was the will of the Creator to go to Teveriah, he would wait in Meron — and when he knew with certainty, he would immediately go. But he did not know.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי מְסַפֵּר כָּל זֶה שֶׁנֵּדַע כַּמָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹהֵב הַתְּמִימוּת.
aligned_segments.en: So he had hisbodidus and pleaded greatly with Hashem to illuminate his thought and understanding as to what to do: "If it is the Creator's will that I go to Teveriah, I travel there at once.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי לֹא הָיִיתִי לַמְדָּן, וְרַק הַתְּמִימוּת בַּלֵּב, אָהַבְתִּי מְאֹד אֶת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְווֹת וְהָאֱמוּנָה וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
aligned_segments.en: I only wish to know the will of the Creator — whether or not, yes or no." He prayed so intensely until Hashem illuminated his eyes and arranged circumstances that he knew with certainty: the will of the Creator was that he go to Teveriah.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאתִי עַל דַּעְתִּי, בְּגִיל שֵׁשׁ-שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים, אָהַבְתִּי מְאֹד אֶת הַתּוֹרָה וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם וֶאֱמוּנָה, אֲבָל הָיָה לִי מְרִירוּת גָּדוֹל, סָבַלְתִּי מְאֹד מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, יֵשׁ יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁרוֹצֶה רַק הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כָּל הַתַּאֲווֹת.
aligned_segments.en: This was on a Wednesday.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם וְאָהַבְתִּי אֶת הַתּוֹרָה מְאֹד.
aligned_segments.en: Rabbi Yisroel arose on Thursday morning early and went to the donkey driver and hired a donkey to Teveriah.

aligned_segments.he: כְּשֶׁרָאִיתִי בֶּן-אָדָם שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לִלְמֹד בְּסֵפֶר וְהוּא מְדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרִים בְּטֵלִים וְלֹא שׁוֹמֵר אֶת הַזְּמַן, אָז אָמַרְתִּי: "מַה זֶּה, הוּא מְשֻׁגָּע.
aligned_segments.en: He could have waited until Sunday after Shabbos.

aligned_segments.he: אִם אֲנִי הָיִיתִי יָכוֹל לִקְרֹא בְּסֵפֶר לֹא הָיִיתִי נָח, לֹא הָיִיתִי בָּטֵל רֶגַע אֶחָד!" וּכְשֶׁרָאִיתִי מִשֶּׁהוּ לוֹמֵד וְהוּא תָּמִים וְהוּא אוֹמֵר תְּהִלִּים, אָז חָשַׁבְתִּי: "אֲהָהּ! זֶה הָאִישׁ הוּא חוֹשֵׁב עַל הַתַּכְלִית הָאֲמִתִּי, זֶה הָאִישׁ - אַשְׁרֵי לוֹ, הוּא עוֹסֵק בִּתְהִלִּים וְלוֹמֵד".
aligned_segments.en: No — since he knew with certainty that the Creator's will was that he go to Teveriah, he went from Tzfas immediately.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי מִתְפַּלֵּל בְּהִתְלַהֲבוּת יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַיְלָדִים.
aligned_segments.en: My parents were poor and ground coffee for a living.

aligned_segments.he: כָּל הַיְלָדִים מִתְפַּלְּלִים, אֲבָל אֲנִי סָפַרְתִּי הַמִּלּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁסּוֹפְרִים כֶּסֶף, וּבְאַהֲבָה וּבִתְמִימוּת.
aligned_segments.en: But during the war the coffee ran out and we were left without livelihood.

aligned_segments.he: וְגַם-כֵּן עוֹד כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי יֶלֶד קָטָן אָהַבְתִּי לִצְעֹק בַּתְּפִלָּה, וְרָאִיתִי שֶׁהַחֲסִידִים לִפְנֵי שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִים בִּצְעָקוֹת הֵם הָיוּ שׁוֹתִים תֵּה אוֹ קָפֶה, אָז אֲנִי הִתְחַלְתִּי לִשְׁתּוֹת יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם וְצָעַקְתִּי יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם.
aligned_segments.en: My mother told her nephew, Binyomin Barzel, that we had no livelihood — and he suggested that she bake bread.

aligned_segments.he: אַחַר-כָּךְ רָאִיתִי שֶׁיְּכוֹלִים לִחְיוֹת בְּלִי תֵּה וְקָפֶה.
aligned_segments.en: She asked him: "From where will I get flour?"

aligned_segments.he: מַה שֶּׁזָּכִיתִי, מַה שֶּׁרָאִיתִי מֵרַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, רָאִיתִי שֶׁהוּא לֹא צָרִיךְ תֵּה, הוּא קָם בַּחֲצוֹת בְּלִי תֵּה בְּלִי קָפֶה.
aligned_segments.en: He said to her: "I will tell the flour merchant to give you as much flour as you need!" And so it was.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, וְגַם-כֵּן עַד הַבַּר-מִצְוָה אֲנִי חִפַּשְׂתִּי רַק לִלְמֹד וּלְקַיֵּם מִצְווֹת וּלְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם וֶאֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה.
aligned_segments.en: We began to bake bread on Sunday — and Rabbi Yisroel arrived in Teveriah that very Thursday. As soon as he descended from the donkey, he needed a loaf of bread to eat his evening meal.

aligned_segments.he: אַחַר-כָּךְ בָּאוּ אֵלַי הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה וִידִידִים וְהִשְׁפִּיעוּ עָלַי וְדִבְּרוּ אִתִּי שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂיתִי בַּר-מִצְוָה אָז אֲנִי צָרִיךְ לִלְמֹד אֵיזֶה מְלָאכָה - חַיָּט אוֹ סַנְדְלָר, וַאֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי: "לֹא, אֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה לִלְמֹד מְלָאכָה, אֲנִי רוֹצֶה רַק תּוֹרָה, רַק תּוֹרָה וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם!"
aligned_segments.en: He met Binyomin Barzel and asked him where to buy a loaf of bread. Binyomin Barzel knew that my family had begun baking bread for sale — and so he brought Rabbi Yisroel to us…

aligned_segments.he: אָז הֵם אָמְרוּ לִי: "אַתָּה צָרִיךְ פַּרְנָסָה וְאַתָּה יֶלֶד, הָאַבָּא לֹא יָכוֹל לָתֵת לְךָ נָדָן וְכֶסֶף, וְגַם-כֵּן אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לְפַרְנֵס אֶת הַבַּיִת".
aligned_segments.en: We were five siblings at home, nearly all older than I — and through Providence Hashem arranged that I took the loaf of bread and went out and gave it to Rabbi Yisroel. The moment I saw him I was tremendously struck — by his countenance and by his manner of speaking. I had never seen such a person. The grace of holiness was upon his face and upon his every word. I was startled and deeply moved. I thought: "Perhaps this is Providence from Hashem — for I had prayed to Hashem! Perhaps this man will be a good thing for me; perhaps salvation will come to me from him; perhaps I will find beside him all that I need." So I thought: "This man is a hidden Tzadik, and beside him I will find what I am searching for — emunah and yiras shomayim."

aligned_segments.he: אָז אָמַרְתִּי: "אֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה לִלְמֹד שׁוּם מְלָאכָה!"
aligned_segments.en: But I thought: "How can I possibly have a connection with him?" I thought he was a hidden Tzadik from among the thirty-six hidden Tzadikim. Such a hidden Tzadik is capable of miraculous travel [k'fitzas haderech] — and tomorrow he could be in Yerushalayim and I would know nothing of him.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי עַקְשָׁן גָּדוֹל וְלֹא לָמַדְתִּי מְלָאכָה, אָז אָמְרוּ הֵם לִי: "מֵאֵיפֹה תִּהְיֶה לְךָ פַּרְנָסָה, הַיְשִׁיבָה לֹא נוֹתֶנֶת פַּרְנָסָה, וְאַתָּה לֹא תִּהְיֶה רַב, אַתָּה לֹא כִּשְׁרוֹנִי".
aligned_segments.en: While I was thinking this, he put his hand into his pocket and took out money to pay me for the bread and said: "Perhaps I could eat the bread here in your house?"

aligned_segments.he: אָז אָמַרְתִּי: "לֶחֶם וּמַיִם זֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַזְמִין לִי".
aligned_segments.en: I felt then that he knew my thought and my desire — I had been thinking how to form a bond with him, and he was asking me: "Perhaps I could eat here in your house?"

aligned_segments.he: אָז הֵם אָמְרוּ לִי: "טוֹב, אַתָּה רוֹצֶה לֶאֱכֹל לֶחֶם וּמַיִם, בְּסֵדֶר, אֲבָל הָאִשָּׁה וְהַיְלָדִים הֵם גַּם-כֵּן?"
aligned_segments.en: Now I saw that this was something distant, because my father would not agree — not because he was unwilling, but because it was already Thursday night and they needed to prepare the challah and bake bread and do all the preparations for Shabbos, to recite Krias Shema and sleep and rise early. And also the house was small with no room even to eat. And my parents were very poor — my father was blind — and the house was like the cave of Rabbi Shimon, with no room to sit. I thought: "My father will rebuke me and shame me — 'What kind of question is this?!'" And I myself could not bring in a guest without my father's permission. But for the sake of having a connection with Rabbi Yisroel, I gathered all my strength with great resolution and said: whatever happens — even if he strikes me and shames me — I will ask my father!

aligned_segments.he: אָז אָמַרְתִּי: "אֲנִי מְקַוֶּה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִתֵּן לִי אִשָּׁה כָּזוֹ שֶׁהִיא גַּם-כֵּן תִּסְתַּפֵּק בְּלֶחֶם וּמַיִם".
aligned_segments.en: So I asked him: "Tatte [Father], take the money for the bread — and this man is asking, he wants to eat the bread here in our home…"

aligned_segments.he: וְאַחַר-כָּךְ כְּשֶׁזָּכִיתִי לְהִתְקָרֵב לְרַבִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְסִפַּרְתִּי לוֹ אֶת הָעִנְיָן,, רָאִיתִי שֶׁהוּא הָיָה נֶהֱנֶה מְאֹד מִזֶּה,
aligned_segments.en: And my father said to me: "Yes, yes, yes! By all means — there is some food left over from our meal: lentils and rice.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי עַד אָז לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מִבְּרֶסְלֶב,, רַק הַלֵּב שֶׁלִּי הָיָה בּוֹעֵר כָּל-כָּךְ לְאַהֲבָה לַתּוֹרָה,, וְהוּא אָמַר לִי: "עָשִׂיתָ טוֹב שֶׁלֹּא לָמַדְתָּ מְלָאכָה!"
aligned_segments.en: Give it to him. Will he eat bread alone?"

aligned_segments.he: וְגַם-כֵּן אֲנִי זוֹכֵר שֶׁהָיִיתִי בֶּן כַּמָּה שָׁנִים אָז הָיִיתִי חוֹלֶה מְאֹד וְהָיָה לִי מִלְחָמָה עִם הַמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, אֲנִי הִרְגַּשְׁתִּי שֶׁאֲנִי עוֹמֵד לָמוּת.
aligned_segments.en: When my father said yes, I saw that this was salvation for me — Providence from Hashem, above the natural order, that I should have a bond with this holy Tzadik. I saw Providence from every direction — this was the highest Providence and a great kindness.

aligned_segments.he: אוֹי, הָיִיתִי חוֹלֶה מְאֹד וְנַעֲשֵׂיתִי חָלָשׁ מְאֹד, וּמִי שֶׁהוּא חוֹלֶה צְרִיכִים לָתֵת לוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ, חָלָב, וְהָאִמָּא נָתְנָה לִי חָלָב עִם מַיִם.
aligned_segments.en: And so it was. They made the evening meal, recited the blessing after eating and Krias Shema, and lay down to sleep on the floor with the children. And Rabbi Yisroel and I remained together alone. He sat beside the doorway on some step of the house, and I gave him bread to eat. He performed netilas yodayim [ritual hand-washing] and recited Hamotzi [the blessing over bread].

aligned_segments.he: אָמַרְתִּי: "תְּנִי לִי חָלָב".
aligned_segments.en: And when I heard the blessing of al netilas yodayim and Hamotzi from him — with such awe and dveykus — I saw that this was true: this was a holy Tzadik, a hidden Tzadik. For his speech was holy — it was like hisbodidus, like prayer. As we speak now — so he was speaking to Hashem; as if there were no other people in the house, only he and Hashem. I saw a wonder. I had grown up among Chassidim, among Torah scholars and God-fearers — but such a blessing I had never heard. And also such a face and countenance as Rabbi Yisroel had — I had never seen.

aligned_segments.he: אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה לָהּ, אָז אָמַרְתִּי לָהּ: "אַתְּ נוֹתֶנֶת לִי חָלָב עִם מַיִם, אֲנִי רוֹצֶה רַק חָלָב!"
aligned_segments.en: I gave him what was left from our meal for him to eat. He said to me: "I do not eat anything — only bread and tea, without sugar." But we had no tea, and we had no kerosene stove — only the wealthy had kerosene stoves; the poor used coals. Making a fire with coals is a craft one must learn, and it took time until I managed and succeeded and made fire and made tea.

aligned_segments.he: אָז הִיא אָמְרָה לִי: "אַתָּה כְּבָר גָּדוֹל, אַתָּה לֹא מִתְבַּיֵּשׁ, מַה זֶּה אִתְּךָ!"
aligned_segments.en: And I did not know that he was from Breslov. I knew only that he was a hidden Tzadik. I could not restrain myself — so in the middle of the work of making the fire, I would go to him every time and whisper to him, in secret, in his ear: "Rabbi Yisroel — know that you came to Teveriah for my sake! For I am in a very difficult situation — the yetzer hora and more is overpowering me — and I greatly desire to serve Hashem in truth, and there are very hard battles upon me. I have been searching all my life for a place to guide me and illuminate within me the light of Hashem, that I should merit to serve Hashem in truth. So I am certain that Hashem sent you to Teveriah, and you came to Teveriah for my sake! And so I beg you — do not abandon me!"

aligned_segments.he: אָז הִתְחַלְתִּי לִבְכּוֹת: "אֲנִי רוֹצֶה חָלָב!"
aligned_segments.en: And he heard such words — and I saw that he was so deeply moved. For he saw with his own eyes the Providence of Hashem in his coming to Teveriah — because the very moment he descended from the donkey and arrived in Teveriah, he came directly to my house, and he was hearing such words! He had needed to travel to Teveriah earlier, but as long as he had not known with certainty that he needed to go, he did not want to move from Meron — he had doubts. Now he saw that this had been the intentional Providence of Hashem that he leave Meron. And I also saw with my own eyes — I saw Rabbi Yisroel and saw what Breslov is!

aligned_segments.he: עַל-כָּל-פָּנִים אַחַר-כָּךְ נַעֲשֵׂיתִי יוֹתֵר טוֹב, אָז אָמַרְתִּי לָאִמָּא: "אֲנִי חָלָשׁ מְאֹד, אֲנִי צָרִיךְ קְצָת בָּשָׂר, מָרָק".
aligned_segments.en: I saw his prayer and his avodah and his Shabbos, his holy words, his desires, and everything he suffered on my behalf. He came to Teveriah and found Yisroel Ber — and then he forgot that he had a family in Tzfas, and that there was Meron, and he cast everything aside only for my sake. And from that very night we merited to form a bond of such a kind — it was an awesome novelty…

aligned_segments.he: הִיא נָתְנָה לִי שְׁלשָׁה מַטְבְּעוֹת, זֶה כְּמוֹ הַיּוֹם שְׁלשָׁה גְּרוּשִׁים. אֲנִי הָלַכְתִּי לַמָּלוֹן וְהַמְּבַשֶּׁלֶת בִּשְּׁלָה טוֹב, אֲבָל הָאִמָּא נָתְנָה לִי שְׁלשָׁה גְּרוּשׁ לִקְנוֹת מָרָק עִם חֲתִיכַת עוֹף, אֲנִי טָעַמְתִּי אֶת הַמָּרָק, אֲנִי לֹא טָעַמְתִּי בַּבַּיִת מָרָק, אָז הִרְגַּשְׁתִּי טַעַם טוֹב, אֲבָל הִיא נָתְנָה לִי אוּלַי שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים אוֹ שְׁלשָׁה פְּעָמִים, אֲנִי הָיִיתִי צָרִיךְ שָׁבוּעַ שְׁבוּעַיִם, וְלֹא הָיָה לָנוּ.
aligned_segments.en: Oy vey, what there was — such a matter, a unique wonder, without parallel.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי חַי בְּנֵס! הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶחֱזִיר לִי הַנְּשָׁמָה בְּנִסִּים!
aligned_segments.en: Afterwards we went and he told me that he wanted to be in some synagogue to say Tikun Chatzos and to recite Tehillim, to pray and to do hisbodidus. So I went with him to the synagogue — and along the way I spoke with him and told him my situation, and he listened to everything. I wanted to confess specific sins before him, and he would not hear of it — he said it was forbidden — only in general. So I spoke with him and wept before him, for I felt that he had healing for me and that he would not abandon me and go to Meron.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים נִסִּים.
aligned_segments.en: And I walked with him from synagogue to synagogue — they were all closed.

aligned_segments.he: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה לִי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לִי בִּשְׁבִיל לִחְיוֹת.
aligned_segments.en: I did not know where the key was. Then it occurred to me that there was only one synagogue of the holy Tzadikim who had lived a hundred years earlier, from the era of the students of the Baal Shem Tov: Rabbi Avrohom Kalisher, and the grandfather of our Rabbenu — Rabbi Nachman Horodanker — and our holy Rabbenu is named after him — and all the rest of the holy Tzadikim.

aligned_segments.he: הָיָה עֲנִיּוּת גָּדוֹל וְהֵם קִבְּלוּ הַכֹּל בְּאַהֲבָה בְּשִׂמְחָה, הָאַבָּא וְהָאִמָּא.
aligned_segments.en: They built this synagogue and took care that it be in a place close to the lake so they could immerse and pray whenever they wished.

aligned_segments.he: אוֹי, אוֹי...
aligned_segments.en: But in winter, when there were heavy rains, the waters would rise and the lake would enter into this synagogue until half the height of the tables — and they could not pray there. So they would take the books and everything and leave the tables in the synagogue, and the synagogue remained open until the month of Nisan, when the waters receded.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי נוֹלַדְתִי בִּטְבֶרְיָה וְהָיִיתִי הֲכִי גָּרוּעַ מִכָּל הַיְלָדִים, נוֹלַדְתִּי בְּבַיִת בַּעֲנִיּוּת כָּזֶה..
aligned_segments.en: So we entered this synagogue — into "the sea" — we climbed up on a table and we learned Torah, Torah lesson number 7, Part 2, in Likutay Moharan [the collected Torah discourses of Rabbenu]: "Ki Merachamom Yenagelem" ["For He who has compassion on them will guide them" — Isaiah 49:10].

aligned_segments.he: יָחִיד בָּעוֹלָם, לֹא הָיָה לִי מַה שֶּׁאֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
aligned_segments.en: He taught me this Torah all night long.

aligned_segments.he: וְגַם-כֵּן אֲנִי הָיִיתִי יֶלֶד חָלָשׁ, אֲנִי יֵשׁ לִי נִסִּים שֶׁאֲנִי חַי וְגַם-כֵּן נִסִּים אֵיךְ שֶׁאֲנִי נִתְגַּדַּלְתִּי. וּכְשֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂיתִי קְצָת יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל, כָּל הַיְלָדִים בָּאוּ עַל פֶּסַח עִם בְּגָדִים חֲדָשִׁים, יָפִים, אֲבָל אֲנִי - הָאַבָּא שֶׁלִּי הָיָה עִוֵּר וְלֹא הָיָה לָהֶם כֶּסֶף וְלֹא הָיָה לִי בֶּגֶד לְחָג.
aligned_segments.en: And I merited — all the days of my life I had not felt the taste of Torah, the taste of yiras shomayim, as on that night when he taught me this holy Torah, "Ki Merachamom Yenagelem." We were in the synagogue and learned all night, and I did not feel at all that one already needed to sleep.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ,, הָאִמָּא שֶׁלִּי עָשְׂתָה הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁלִּי כְּמוֹ חָדָשׁ,, הִיא כִּבְּסָה וְסִידְּרָה אוֹתוֹ וַאֲנִי שָׂמַחְתִּי מְאֹד,
aligned_segments.en: He was "wealthy" — he had candles and matches, which were very precious.

aligned_segments.he: וּכְשֶׁבָּאתִי לְבֵית-הַכְּנֶסֶת - כָּל הַיְלָדִים בָּאוּ עִם בְּגָדִים חֲדָשִׁים,, וַאֲנִי בָּאתִי לְבֵית-הַכְּנֶסֶת כְּמוֹ כָּל הַיְלָדִים עִם בֶּגֶד יָפֶה מְאֹד,
aligned_segments.en: He lit a candle and studied with me in Likutay Moharan until nearly dawn — until I heard the sound of my mother weeping bitterly, like one after a passing, crying: "My son, my son, my son!" She saw that it was nearly daylight and I was nowhere to be found.

aligned_segments.he: לֹא חָדָשׁ,, אֲבָל הָיָה לִי בֶּגֶד כְּמוֹ חָדָשׁ.
aligned_segments.en: She thought: "Who knows what happened?!"

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי, הָאַבָּא שֶׁלִּי הָיָה עָנִי וְלֹא הָיָה לִי כֶּסֶף, הִתְבַּיַּשְׁתִּי לָבוֹא בְּלִי כֶּסֶף לְהָרַבִּי.
aligned_segments.en: She went from synagogue to synagogue to search for me, weeping and wailing — and found nothing. The synagogues were closed; she did not know where the key was.

aligned_segments.he: מַה, זֶה כָּל הַפַּרְנָסָה שֶׁלּוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: She cried loudly and her voice was heard throughout the city. Teveriah was a small city and the entire city came out.

aligned_segments.he: בְּרֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ צְרִיכִים לָבוֹא עִם כֶּסֶף, כָּל הַיְלָדִים הֵבִיאוּ כֶּסֶף לְהָרַבִּי, אֲנִי נִתְבַּיַּשְׁתִּי, הָלַכְתִּי לְהָרַבִּי בְּלִי כֶּסֶף, "אֵיךְ בָּאִים בְּלִי כֶּסֶף כַּאֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ רֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ?!" אֵין דָּבָר כָּזֶה.
aligned_segments.en: They thought that someone had passed away. The neighbors from the area came in the morning and asked: "What — what is all this crying and screaming? What happened?!"

aligned_segments.he: אוֹי הַגֵּיהִנָּם שֶׁלִּי שֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לַבֵּית-סֵפֶר לְהָרַבִּי בְּלִי כֶּסֶף, בְּכָל פְּסִיעָה הִרְגַּשְׁתִּי גֵּיהִנָּם.
aligned_segments.en: She told them: "Some man came and bought bread from us and ate the bread in our home — and he took Yisroel Ber and went the whole night and disappeared.

aligned_segments.he: כָּל הַתַּלְמִידִים בָּאוּ בְּרֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ עִם כֶּסֶף, רַק אֲנִי בָּאתִי בְּלִי כֶּסֶף.
aligned_segments.en: I got up to work and Yisroel Ber is gone!" And they did not know who it was.

aligned_segments.he: תַּלְמִיד יָחִיד!
aligned_segments.en: It was the beginning of the war, and the Turks were wild men — they would simply see any man who had hands and feet and conscript him into the army. So she thought: "Perhaps… I have hands and feet, so perhaps they took him into the army."

aligned_segments.he: הָרַבִּי אָמַר לִי: "מָה אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה, מַדּוּעַ אַתָּה בָּא? כָּל הַחֹדֶשׁ אֲנִי מְצַפֶּה עַל רֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ וְהָיָה רֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ וּבָאתָ בְּלִי כֶּסֶף.
aligned_segments.en: She wept and the whole city was in an uproar.

aligned_segments.he: זֶה כָּל הַפַּרְנָסָה שֶׁלִּי, רֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ כָּל הַתַּלְמִידִים מְבִיאִים לִי כֶּסֶף וְיֵשׁ לִי פַּרְנָסָה, וְאַתָּה יֶלֶד יָחִיד שֶׁלֹּא מֵבִיא כֶּסֶף, לֹא הֵבֵאתָ כֶּסֶף!"
aligned_segments.en: And I heard it. I said to Rabbi Yisroel: "Oy vey — it is already past midnight and my mother is searching, pleading for me!"

aligned_segments.he: יֵשׁ כְּבָר יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה שָׁנִים וַאֲנִי זוֹכֵר אֶת זֶה כְּמוֹ עַכְשָׁו. הוּא אָמַר לִי: "מַדּוּעַ בָּאתָ רֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ בְּלִי כֶּסֶף? מַה זֶּה? תַּגִּיד לְהָאַבָּא, בְּרֹאשׁ-חֹדֶשׁ צְרִיכִים לְהָבִיא כֶּסֶף!"
aligned_segments.en: I came out of the synagogue and went to my mother and said: "What is this weeping about?"

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי - הָיָה לִי דָּבָר גָּדוֹל, הַטַּעַם שֶׁלִּי הָיָה טַעַם גֵּיהִנָּם, אֵיךְ אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לַחֵדֶר לְהָרַבִּי בְּלִי כֶּסֶף, אֲנִי לֹא הָיָה לִי.
aligned_segments.en: She said to me: "What have you done?!

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי בָּאתִי לְמָחֳרַת גַּם-כֵּן בְּלִי כֶּסֶף...
aligned_segments.en: Where did you go the whole night?! In any case — know that now we must throw away all the dough, all the challah, and all the bread."

aligned_segments.he: וְכֵן הָיָה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, אֲנִי נוֹלַדְתִּי וְהָיָה לִי אַהֲבָה לַעֲזֹר לָעֲנִיִּים וְאָהַבְתִּי מְאֹד מִצְוָה, וְאַף-עַל-פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָדַעְתִּי אֲבָל הִרְגַּשְׁתִּי שֶׁמִּצְוַת צְדָקָה זֶה דָּבָר גָּדוֹל מְאֹד, זֶה מִצְוָה קְדוֹשָׁה מְאֹד וְזֶה נוֹרָא מְאֹד.
aligned_segments.en: And from that night there was a great commotion in Teveriah: "This night, Yisroel Ber became a Breslover!"

aligned_segments.he: בִּטְבֶרְיָה הָיָה אִישׁ זָקֵן גָּדוֹל שְׁמוֹ הָיָה הָרַב יוֹסֵף נֹחַ. וְהוּא הָיָה עָנִי וְהָיָה לוֹ אִשָּׁה וְהָיָה לָהֶם חֶדֶר עַל-יָדִי בְּאֵיזֶה חָצֵר, וְהוּא הָיָה מַחֲזִיר עַל הַפְּתָחִים. יֵשׁ עֲנִיִּים שֶׁלֹּא מַחֲזִירִים עַל הַפְּתָחִים, הֵם עֲנִיִּים אֲבָל נוֹתְנִים לָהֶם בְּכָבוֹד אֵיזֶה מַטְבֵּעַ, אֵיזֶה צְדָקָה, אֲבָל הוּא הָיָה מַחֲזִיר עַל הַפְּתָחִים, וַאֲנִי רָאִיתִי שֶׁהוּא מַחֲזִיר עַל הַפְּתָחִים, אָז הָיָה לִי רַחֲמָנוּת גָּדוֹל עָלָיו, "מִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ מַה לֶּאֱכֹל אֵיזֶה חֲתִיכַת לֶחֶם". אֲנִי זוֹכֵר עַד הַיּוֹם הַשֵּׁם שֶׁלּוֹ - יוֹסֵף נֹחַ, שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת, זֶה הָיָה בְּפָרָשַׁת נֹחַ.
aligned_segments.en: In the morning I went to the synagogue — and Rabbi Yisroel was in the synagogue — and I spoke with him and we studied Rabbenu's books, Gemora, and Shulchan Aruch [Code of Jewish Law], and immediately a great tumult arose in Teveriah and it became known that I had become a Breslover.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי נוֹלַדְתִּי בְּבַיִת עִם עֲנִיּוּת כָּזֶה שֶׁאֵין בָּעוֹלָם, וְהַחֲתִיכַת לֶחֶם הָיָה אוֹצָר.
aligned_segments.en: And I had opposition and great battle.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, אֲנִי הָיִיתִי יֶלֶד טוֹב, אָז בַּבֹּקֶר שֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לַחֶדֶר לִלְמֹד, אָז הָאִמָּא נָתְנָה לִי פְּרוּסַת לֶחֶם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִי לֶאֱכֹל עַד הַצָּהֳרַיִם, אוּלַי אֶהְיֶה רָעֵב, וְהִיא נָתְנָה לִי כַּמָּה טִפּוֹת שֶׁמֶן עַל הַלֶּחֶם וַאֲנִי שָׂמַחְתִּי מְאֹד, לָקַחְתִּי אֶת הַלֶּחֶם וּבִקַּשְׁתִּי אוֹתָהּ: "אִמָּא, תְּנִי עוֹד כַּמָּה, שְׁנַיִם אוֹ שְׁלשָׁה טִפּוֹת".
aligned_segments.en: My father and mother and relatives and the family and the entire yeshiva — all of them said: "Oy vey, what a pity — Yisroel Ber has become a Breslover, Yisroel Ber has become a Breslover!" All of them opposed.

aligned_segments.he: וְזֶה הָיָה יוֹם חֲמִישִׁי, אָז הִיא צָעֲקָה עָלַי: "אֲנִי צְרִיכָה אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן בִּשְׁבִיל שַׁבָּת, כָּל הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא הַשֶּׁמֶן. אִם אֲנִי אֶתֵּן לְךָ עוֹד טִפָּה אָז לֹא יִהְיֶה מַסְפִּיק שֶׁמֶן לַצּ'וּלֶנְט, וְאַתָּה רוֹצֶה עוֹד טִפָּה? אַל תְּדַבֵּר כְּלוּם. זֶה מַסְפִּיק!"
aligned_segments.en: They went from the yeshiva to my parents and told them: "Do you know — Yisroel Ber has become a Breslover."

aligned_segments.he: נוּ,, אָז אֲנִי רָצִיתִי לַעֲשׂוֹת צְדָקָה וָחֶסֶד,, לֹא הָיָה לִי כֶּסֶף,, אָז לָקַחְתִּי אֶת הַפְּרוּסַת הַלֶּחֶם,, וּכְשֶׁהָלַכְתִּי בַּבֹּקֶר לַחֵדֶר שֶׁלּוֹמְדִים הַיְלָדִים,
aligned_segments.en: My father and mother heard — and were not so alarmed.

aligned_segments.he: אָז אַף אֶחָד לֹא יָדַע,, וַאֲנִי הָלַכְתִּי לְהַיְהוּדִי הַזָּקֵן הַזֶּה וְהוּא לֹא הָיָה בַּבַּיִת,, וְחִפַּשְׂתִּי וְהָלַכְתִּי אֵלָיו וְנָתַתִּי לוֹ וְהוּא לָקַח מִמֶּנִּי, וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי כָּל-כָּךְ שָׂמֵחַ שֶׁזָּכִיתִי לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוַת צְדָקָה - נָתַתִּי לוֹ לֶחֶם לֶאֱכֹל.
aligned_segments.en: But then the gabbai of the yeshiva came, and other distinguished men, scholars and men of reputation, and said to my father: "Do you know that Yisroel Ber has become a Breslover?!"

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי רָצִיתִי לְקַיֵּם מִצְוַת צְדָקָה, לְרַחֵם עַל עָנִי, אָז אֲנִי הָלַכְתִּי וְנָתַתִּי לוֹ בְּשִׂמְחָה אֶת הַלֶּחֶם עִם הַטִּפּוֹת שֶׁמֶן זַיִת.
aligned_segments.en: My father said: "I am not worried.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי נָתַתִּי לוֹ, אֲנִי חָשַׁבְתִּי שֶׁאֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי צְדָקָה גְּדוֹלָה, הוּא וְאִשְׁתּוֹ הֵם יֹאכְלוּ.
aligned_segments.en: I know my son — he is God-fearing and fulfills the commandment of honoring his father in the most exemplary way in the world.

aligned_segments.he: וְזֶה הָיָה בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, וַאֲנִי כְּבָר הִתְחַלְתִּי לִלְמֹד חֻמָּשׁ, אָז הַמִּנְהָג שֶׁל הָרַבִּי הָיָה שֶׁבְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן הוּא הָיָה מְסַפֵּר לַתַּלְמִידִים: "יְלָדִים, אַתֶּם יוֹדְעִים, הַשָּׁבוּעַ הוֹלֵך הַפָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ".
aligned_segments.en: If I send him into fire he would go. There is no one like him.

aligned_segments.he: הוּא אָמַר אֶת זֶה כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ שֶׁזֶּה פָּרָשַׁת 'נֹחַ', אָז הֵם שָׁמְעוּ שֶׁהַשָּׁבוּעַ צְרִיכִים לִלְמֹד פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ.
aligned_segments.en: I am not worried.

aligned_segments.he: אַחַר-כָּךְ הוּא סִפֵּר לָהֶם כַּמָּה רָאשֵׁי פְּרָקִים מֵהַלִּמּוּד שֶׁצְּרִיכִים, כַּמָּה סִפּוּרִים מֵהַפָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ, כַּמָּה גֹּדֶל הַתֵּיבָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת הַלִּמּוּד הֵם כְּבָר יֵדְעוּ אֵיזֶה דְּבָרִים.
aligned_segments.en: When he comes home from the yeshiva I will tell him that I don't want it — and he will not be a Breslover. I have no problem."

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הָאֲכִילָה. כָּל הַתַּלְמִידִים בָּאוּ לַחֵדֶר עִם לֶחֶם וְעִם שֶׁמֶן זַיִת וַאֲנִי לֹא הָיָה לִי לֹא לֶחֶם וְלֹא שֶׁמֶן זַיִת, אֲנִי נָתַתִּי לְהֶעָנִי הַזֶּה וְהָיִיתִי רָעֵב מְאֹד וְלֹא יָכֹלְתִּי לְהַכְנִיס בְּלִבִּי אֶת הַדִּבּוּרִים שֶׁדִּבֵּר הָרַבִּי, אֲנִי הָיִיתִי בַּשֻּׁלְחָן אֲבָל הָיִיתִי רָעֵב וְלֹא יָדַעְתִּי כְּלָל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְדַבֵּר. מַה לַּעֲשׂוֹת, אֲנִי לֹא יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל, אֲנִי רָעֵב. הָיָה כּוֹאֵב לִי הָרֹאשׁ מְאֹד, אֲנִי הָיִיתִי צָרִיךְ לֶאֱכֹל וְאֵין לִי. וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי בְּטֶבַע גּוּף חָלָשׁ, וּמִגֹּדֶל הַחֲלִישׁוּת לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי כְּלָל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְסַפֵּר שֶׁהַשָּׁבוּעַ פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ. וְהוּא רָצָה לָדַעַת אֵיזֶה יְלָדִים טוֹבִים וְאֵיזֶה יְלָדִים לֹא טוֹבִים, אָז פִּתְאוֹם הוּא עָמַד וְשָׁאַל אֶת יֶלֶד זֶה: "תַּגִּיד, אֵיזֶה פָּרָשָׁה הַשָּׁבוּעַ?" וּכְשֶׁהַיֶּלֶד יָדַע שֶׁהַשָּׁבוּעַ פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ אָז הוּא יֶלֶד טוֹב. אֲבָל הָיוּ יְלָדִים שֶׁלֹּא זָכְרוּ וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְקַבֵּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּזְכְּרוּ שֶׁפָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ. אָז הוּא הִסְתַּכֵּל עַל כָּל הַתַּלְמִידִים וְהוּא הִבְחִין בִּי שֶׁאֲנִי לֹא שׁוֹמֵעַ כְּלָל וְלֹא יוֹדֵעַ כְּלָל, כְּאִלּוּ אֲנִי לֹא נִמְצָא. הוּא בָּא אֵלַי, "יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער, תַּגִּיד לִי, אֵיזֶה פָּרָשָׁה הַשָּׁבוּעַ?" אֲנִי לֹא יָדַעְתִּי כְּלוּם, כְּאִלּוּ אֲנִי לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּאִלּוּ אֲנִי בִּמְדִינָה אַחֶרֶת.
aligned_segments.en: They said: "You don't know what Breslov is. He will not listen to you. You need a heavy battle."

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, הוּא מְחַכֶּה וּמְצַפֶּה אוּלַי אֲנִי אֶזְכֹּר, אֲנִי לֹא יוֹדֵעַ כְּלוּם. הוּא חִכָּה וְחִכָּה עַל תְּשׁוּבָה.. וְאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה, אֲנִי לֹא יוֹדֵעַ!
aligned_segments.en: He said: "I am not worried. I know my son."

aligned_segments.he: אָז הוּא שָׁאַל אוֹתִי: "אֵיפֹה הָיִיתָ! לֹא הָיִיתָ פֹּה בִּכְלַל! בְּאֵיזֶה עוֹלָם הָיִיתָ! מַה זֶּה, אֲנִי מְדַבֵּר וַאֲנִי נוֹתֵן כָּל הַכֹּחַ שֶׁלִּי וְאַתָּה לֹא שׁוֹמֵעַ?"
aligned_segments.en: I came from the yeshiva on Thursday — and my father said to me: "Know, my son, that the leaders of the yeshiva were here and told me that you have become a Breslover. Know, my son — have mercy on me! I beg of you not to cause me pain. You belong to a different Chassidus. I give you permission to be in whatever Chassidus you wish — I have only one request: I do not want you to be a Breslover."

aligned_segments.he: אָז הוּא הִכָּה אוֹתִי, "יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער, תַּגִּיד אֵיזֶה פָּרָשָׁה אֲנַחְנוּ!"
aligned_segments.en: This was the first time in my life that I transgressed the commandment of honoring my father — and I said to him: "Father, you know me — I fulfill the commandment of honoring my father. Everything I will listen to you in. But this one thing — no! In this I will not listen to you! Why? I do not know."

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי לֹא שׁוֹמֵעַ, הָרֹאשׁ הָיָה כּוֹאֵב לִי וְלֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אוֹמֵר כְּלָל.
aligned_segments.en: He saw: "Ahh — they were right. They said I don't know what Breslov is!

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי לֹא יָדַעְתִּי כְּלָל אִם פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ, אִם יֵשׁ נֹחַ, אִם יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה, אִם יֵשׁ פָּרָשָׁה, לֹא יָדַעְתִּי כְּלוּם.
aligned_segments.en: What is this! This is very frightening — he has fulfilled the commandment of honoring his father with mesiras nefesh all the days of his life, and now he speaks like this?! This is the first time in my life I hear that he does not want to fulfill my word."

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, נוּ, הָיָה לִי גֵּיהִנָּם, הָיִיתִי יֶלֶד קָטָן וְהָיָה לִי כְּבָר שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים גֵּיהִנָּם...
aligned_segments.en: My father said to me: "I do not want you to be in Breslov — in any way! I want you to be like everyone else."

aligned_segments.he: וְהָרַבִּי הָיָה כַּעֲסָן.
aligned_segments.en: Oy, oy — what there was still, what there was!

aligned_segments.he: הוּא הָיָה בְּכַעַס גָּדוֹל עָלַי, וְהוּא הָיָה זָקֵן וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי יֶלֶד, הוּא הִכָּה אוֹתִי בְּאַכְזָרִיּוּת כָּזֶה, "מַה זֶּה, אֲנִי מְדַבֵּר בְּחִנָּם, אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים כָּכָה שֶׁהַשָּׁבוּעַ פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ וְאַתָּה לֹא יוֹדֵעַ אֲפִלּוּ אֵיזֶה דִּבּוּר אֶחָד.
aligned_segments.en: Can it be told?! All of Teveriah wept over me.

aligned_segments.he: אַתָּה לֹא מֵשִׂים לֵב, לֹא מְקַבֵּל וְלֹא יוֹדֵעַ, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא הָיִיתָ פֹּה, כְּאִלּוּ אֵין רַבִּי.
aligned_segments.en: My father and mother wept: "What has become of him, what is this?!

aligned_segments.he: מַה זֶּה, אֵיפֹה הָיִיתָ!"
aligned_segments.en: One cannot be a Chassid of Breslov! What is this — we don't want Breslov!"

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי שֶׁאֲנִי צָרִיךְ אֶת הַלֶּחֶם כִּי אֲנִי מְקַבֵּל מַכּוֹת וְהָיָה לִי צַעַר, וְגַם-כֵּן הָיָה לִי בּוּשָׁה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁאֲנִי תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹדֵעַ כְּלוּם. אֲנִי הִתְבַּיַּשְׁתִּי בִּפְנֵי כָּל הַתַּלְמִידִים, הוּא לֹא הִכָּה אַף יֶלֶד אֶחָד - רַק אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּער. הוּא כָּל-כָּךְ הִכָּה אוֹתִי בְּאַכְזָרִיּוּת, וְהַבִּזְיוֹנוֹת הֵבִיאוּ לִי יוֹתֵר צַעַר מֵהַמַּכּוֹת.
aligned_segments.en: My father, mother and family said: "This is impossible — this can only be sorcery.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי הָיִיתִי תָּמִיד בְּיִסּוּרִים וּבִפְחָדִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁאַל הָרַבִּי אֵיזֶה פָּרָשָׁה. נוּ, מַה יִּהְיֶה? אֲנִי אֲקַבֵּל צְעָקוֹת וּמַכּוֹת. אוֹי, כְּשֶׁהוּא שָׁאַל אֵיזֶה פָּרָשַׁה הַשָּׁבוּעַ, אֲנִי הִרְגַּשְׁתִּי שֶׁאֲנִי מְאַבֵּד הַלֵּב, שֶׁאֲנִי מְאַבֵּד כָּל הַחַיִּים, כִּי לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מַה הוּא מְדַבֵּר. אוֹי, אוֹי...
aligned_segments.en: Breslov is sorcery!"

aligned_segments.he: אָמַרְתִּי: "מֵהַיּוֹם אֲנִי כְּבָר לֹא אֶתֵּן אֶת הַלֶּחֶם, אִם לֹא - אֲנִי אֲקַבֵּל מַכּוֹת, אֲנִי לֹא אֵדַע אִם הַשָּׁבוּעַ פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ". אַף-עַל-פִּי-כֵן, נָתַתִּי עוֹד פַּעַם לֶעָנִי הַזֶּה אֶת הַלֶּחֶם.
aligned_segments.en: And so it was with everyone — all the scholars laughed: "Breslov, Breslov, Breslov…"

aligned_segments.he: וְהָיָה אֶצְלִי כָּל הַיַּהֲדוּת,, הַכָּל מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מֵעִנְיַן רוּחָנִי,, מֵעִנְיַן אֱמוּנָה,, מֵעִנְיַן הַתּוֹרָה - קִבַּלְתִּי יְדִיעוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת מַה שֶׁלֹּא יָדַעְתִּי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵהַתּוֹרָה,
aligned_segments.en: Rabbi Yisroel Kardoner said to my mother: "This is something that cannot be undone in any way.

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי שׁוֹמֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ תּוֹרָה וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,, אָז הָיָה לִי שִׂמְחָה גְּדוֹלָה.
aligned_segments.en: Yisroel Ber will be in Breslov for ever and ever — and so it will be!"

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי פָּשׁוּט מְאֹד וְהָיָה לִי רָצוֹן חָזָק לִהְיוֹת אִישׁ כָּשֵׁר בֶּאֱמֶת, לַעֲבֹד הַשֵּׁם בֶּאֱמֶת וְלִלְמֹד וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל.
aligned_segments.en: My mother heard him say this — and she fell and died from the enormity of the fear and the great shock, at the home of Rabbi Yisroel.

aligned_segments.he: בִּפְרָט שֶׁהִתְחִיל הַשָּׁנִים שֶׁל אַחֲרֵי בַּר-מִצְוָה, הִתְחִיל הַמִּלְחָמָה שֶׁל חַטֹּאת נְעוּרִים, מַחֲשָׁבוֹת, וְלֹא יָדַעְתִּי מַה זֶּה.
aligned_segments.en: She passed away.

aligned_segments.he: נוּ, נוּ, מִי יָכוֹל לְסַפֵּר מִי יָכוֹל לְשַׁעֵר...
aligned_segments.en: She heard that no power in the world would help. I said: "I will be in Breslov all the days of my life!"

aligned_segments.he: הָיָה לִי מִלְחָמוֹת קָשׁוֹת וְהָיָה לִי כָּל פְּגָם כָּלְשֶׁהוּ מֵהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, הָיָה אֶצְלִי כְּמוֹ הָאִישׁ הָכִי רָשָׁע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
aligned_segments.en: And then a miracle occurred from Heaven.

aligned_segments.he: וּמָצָאתִי לִי מָקוֹם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לַתּוֹרָה.
aligned_segments.en: One member of the Chevra Kaddisha [burial society] saw that my mother made some movement with her eye — a sign of life.

aligned_segments.he: דַּוְקָא מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלַי - זֶה הֵבִיא אוֹתִי לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אֲנִי הִתְגַּבַּרְתִּי, לָחַמְתִּי וְאָמַרְתִּי: "אֲנִי אוֹהֵב אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִהְיֶה אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה, אֲנִי רוֹצֶה לַעֲבֹד הַשֵּׁם!"
aligned_segments.en: He saw that the eye was not dead. But he thought: "This must be mere imagination."

aligned_segments.he: אוֹי, רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם...
aligned_segments.en: Then another man came and also saw the same thing — that she made some movement with her eye. "By the testimony of two witnesses shall a matter be established!" [Devarim 19:15]

aligned_segments.he: אֲנִי הִתְפַּלַּלְתִּי בְּבֵית-כְּנֶסֶת, אֲבָל אֲנִי הִתְפַּלַּלְתִּי בְּהִתְלַהֲבוּת בֶּאֱמוּנָה וּבֶאֱמֶת, וַאֲנִי הָיִיתִי יָחִיד בָּזֶה, וְהָיִיתִי נִרְאֶה כְּמוֹ מְשֻׁגָּע, הָיִיתִי צוֹעֵק מַמָּשׁ עַד לֶב-הַשָּׁמַיִם.
aligned_segments.en: The people said it was impossible for her to be alive — her heart had ceased to beat and everyone had seen that she died.

aligned_segments.he: כֻּלָּם צָעֲקוּ, כִּי כָּל מִי שֶׁצָּעַק יוֹתֵר הוּא הָיָה חָסִיד יוֹתֵר, הָיָה יוֹתֵר חָשׁוּב, וַאֲנִי צָעַקְתִּי יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם, אֲבָל אֲנִי לֹא הִתְכַּוַּנְתִּי בִּשְׁבִיל חֲשִׁיבוּת אוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל אֵיזֶה פְּנִיָּה, רַק אֲנִי - הַלֵּב שֶׁלִּי הָיָה בּוֹעֵר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וַאֲנִי צָעַקְתִּי בְּקוֹלוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ...
aligned_segments.en: But she said: "No, I am not dead…"

aligned_segments.he: וְעַל-יָדִי יָשַׁב זָקֵן גָּדוֹל, הָיָה לוֹ זָקָן יָפֶה, שְׁמוֹ רַב קְהָת, וַאֲנִי יָשַׁבְתִּי עַל-יָדוֹ וְצָעַקְתִּי: "הוֹדוּ לַשֵּׁם כִּי טוֹב, כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ".
aligned_segments.en: And the whole Chassidic community and the whole city was already seething. Who had the courage to speak with a Breslov Chassid or to read a Breslov book — he was afraid. Why would he do that — it was not his business. And blessed be Hashem — I paid no attention, I looked at nothing: neither at great rabbis nor at a prospective match. I gave over everything — only from what I had seen: what Rabbi Yisroel Kardoner was.

aligned_segments.he: וְהוּא אַחֲרֵי הַתְּפִלָּה הָיָה צוֹעֵק עָלַי וּבוֹכֶה: "מָה אַתָּה רוֹצֶה מִמֶּנִּי, אַתָּה רוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת לִי חֵרֵשׁ וַאֲנִי לֹא אֶשְׁמַע כְּלוּם, מַדּוּעַ אַתָּה צוֹעֵק בְּקוֹלוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ, אַתָּה תַּהֲרֹג אוֹתִי, אַתָּה תַּהֲרֹג אוֹתִי, זֶה לֹא צְעָקָה, זֶה בִּשְׁבִיל לַהֲרֹג!"
aligned_segments.en: Until today I have a reputation — it has already been eighty years since I drew close to Rabbi Yisroel, and all of them opposed in such a way — and I, blessed be Hashem, received all the volleys, all the contempt and all the troubles with love, with great courage — and all of it was annulled. They saw my courage — it was not natural; they could not understand it.

aligned_segments.he: הוּא הָיָה בֶּן-תּוֹרָה וִירֵא שָׁמַיִם, אֲבָל הוּא לֹא יָכוֹל לִסְבֹּל אֶת הַצְּעָקוֹת, הוּא הָיָה סוֹבֵל מִזֶּה צַעַר גָּדוֹל.
aligned_segments.en: I saw from one great Torah scholar and learned with him. Now, it would have been a miracle if he had said: "Breslov — no" — and I would have had to immediately abandon it.

aligned_segments.he: הַהַקְפָּדָה שֶׁלּוֹ וְהַכַּעַס שֶׁלּוֹ אֲנִי זוֹכֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד עַכְשָׁו אֶצְלִי וְצוֹעֵק עָלַי: "מָה אַתָּה רוֹצֶה מִמֶּנִּי!"
aligned_segments.en: But I had seen what I had seen. I saw Rabbi Yisroel — I only saw him for the first time in my life, did not know who he was — and I said: "Oy vey, this man is a hidden Tzadik and I need him greatly. If only I could form some bond with him, I would merit serving Hashem in truth as I desire."

aligned_segments.he: מִי יָכוֹל לְשַׁעֵר, מִי יָכוֹל לְתָאֵר...
aligned_segments.en: What passed over me and over Rabbi Yisroel — what we suffered…

aligned_segments.he: וְלֹא הָיָה לִי מִי שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר אִתִּי מִי שֶׁיְּחַנֵּךְ אוֹתִי, הָיִיתִי תָּמִיד בְּעַצְבוּת, שָׁבוּר, אֲבָל זֶה הָיָה טוֹבָה גְּדוֹלָה, כִּי הָיִיתִי שָׁבוּר וְזֶה הִקְרִיב אוֹתִי לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לַתּוֹרָה, זֶה הָיָה לְטוֹבָה.
aligned_segments.en: The main point: how Hashem arranged the circumstances, how I merited to come to know of Rabbenu. At the very outset I knew nothing of Rabbenu, knew nothing of the name Breslov — He arranged that I come to know that there were Breslov books that it was forbidden to read! And I was a poor, oppressed child — not talented; I had no head for learning. In any case, from that night — and blessed be Hashem, until this day — I have held firm.

aligned_segments.he: וְהִתְגַּעְגַּעְתִּי, הָיָה לִי גַּעְגּוּעִים לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
aligned_segments.en: They all laughed at me — the great ones and all the rabbis: "He is Breslov!" But I laughed at all of them. I defeated them all. I remained — and I will remain — on this path. And Hashem gives me the gift of still being in this world…
